claim: Modern (post-2012) high-capacity neural networks are poorly calibrated despite higher accuracy, unlike smaller neural networks from a decade earlier, with network depth, width, weight decay, and Batch Normalization identified as key contributing factors.
stance_target: Model capacity/architecture choices systematically degrade calibration even as accuracy improves
scope_conditions: Image and document classification, state-of-the-art architectures circa 2017
quoted_support: We discover that modern neural networks, unlike those from a decade ago, are poorly calibrated. Through extensive experiments, we observe that depth, width, weight decay, and Batch Normalization are important factors influencing calibration.

claim: Temperature scaling, a single-parameter variant of Platt scaling, is surprisingly effective at calibrating neural network predictions on most datasets, providing a simple practical recipe for post-hoc calibration.
stance_target: Simple single-parameter rescaling methods are competitive with more complex calibration techniques
scope_conditions: Post-processing calibration methods evaluated on state-of-the-art image/document classification architectures
quoted_support: on most datasets, temperature scaling -- a single-parameter variant of Platt Scaling -- is surprisingly effective at calibrating predictions.
